tts: Every morning, you carry out a bucket whose contents are best not to think about. Time to automate this.
So you cut a hole in the floor and put a pipe under the bucket that runs down into a ditch. Nothing to carry anymore. It all just goes away.
But the smell coming up that pipe is unbearable. So you bend the pipe into a U. A little water always sits in the bend and blocks the smell, like a plug.
But the contents won't reach the bend on their own. They need a push. So you hang a tank of water up high, pull a chain, and the rush of water carries everything away.
Then the tank is empty, and hauling water is a chore. So you connect it to the water supply and add a float: as the tank fills, the float rises and shuts the valve by itself.
You swap the bucket for a smooth porcelain bowl, so nothing sticks, and add a seat on top, for comfort.
Congrats, you just invented the flush toilet. John Harington built one for Queen Elizabeth the First in fifteen ninety-six, and Alexander Cumming patented the bent pipe in seventeen seventy-five.
So appreciate it: more than three billion people still don't have safe toilets. And it all started with a bucket.
